# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.29 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.28. Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine. The automated test suite also passes on CI runners for Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64 and macOS Apple-silicon; **nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64, and no photo batch was processed there**.

**Fixed (found by an adversarial audit of the pre.28 code)**
- **`--trim-background` could wipe a whole page.** Only the largest blob of paper was kept, so a dark gutter or a banner that split the sheet in two made the smaller piece white. Now every big blob counts as paper. (`phone-photos` was not affected: it cuts the spread before trimming.)
- **`--dry-run` no longer creates output folders.**
- **`--pages 4-`** past the last page now says "no page left".
- **"All options" window**: Stop no longer blocks and shows "stopped" instead of "exit -1"; closing the window or the app stops the running command.
- `--find-replace` rules and the OCR retry are hardened against degenerate input; the release guide check matches the version exactly (`pre.2` no longer matches `pre.28`).

**Faster** (6 phone photos, `phone-photos-a4`, 2 cores: 13.1 s → 9.3 s)
- Fit-to-page and output scaling run on all cores (0.82 s → 0.09 s per page); results match the previous filter to within one grey level.
- `sharpen`'s blur is 25 % faster with identical output; `box_filter` is O(n) (identical output).
- `--timings` now lists perspective, fingers, trim, normalize, sharpen, resize and image encoding separately.

**Verified**: unit tests (including a regression test for the split sheet, equality tests against reference implementations) and clippy; the timings above on one machine.
**Not verified**: real photos on Windows, macOS and arm64 (only the unit tests run there); machines with more than 2 cores; the new code on a full 113-photo batch (only the 6-photo run was repeated).

**Known limits** (unchanged): photos that are not pages are kept; a large hand holding the page can stay; small notches where a finger was removed; a folded page corner can be cut diagonally; tables and contents pages read few words; OCR can misread characters such as `@`.
